questions.q: How long did the Great Indian Peninsula Railway take to cross from Bombay to Calcutta?
choices: Three days
Ten days
Two weeks
One day and a night
questions.evidence: traverses the peninsula from Bombay to Calcutta in three days

questions.q: Why is the railway trip across India longer than the straight distance between Bombay and Calcutta?
choices: The trains stop for a whole day in every large town
The railway does not run in a direct line
The trains must go back and forth over the same hills
The line goes north to the mountains and back down
questions.evidence: This railway does not run in a direct line across India.

questions.q: What did Fogg do about the famous sights of Bombay?
choices: He hired a guide to show him the city hall
He did not care in the least to see any of them
He sent Passepartout to sketch them in a notebook for him
He visited only the pagoda on Malabar Hill before dinner
questions.evidence: he cared not a straw to see them

questions.q: When Fogg asked whether the "rabbit" had mewed when it was killed, what did he suspect?
choices: That the meat was really from a cat, not a rabbit
That the rabbit had been cooked far too long
That the landlord had stolen the rabbit from a farm
That the spiced sauce was hiding spoiled meat
questions.evidence: And this rabbit did not mew when he was killed?

questions.q: Why couldn't Fix arrest Fogg as soon as they reached Bombay?
choices: Fogg had already left on an earlier train for Calcutta
The warrant from London had not yet reached Bombay
The Bombay police said Fogg was clearly an honest man
Fix had lost the robber's description on the steamer
questions.evidence: It had not reached the office; indeed, there had not yet been time for it to arrive.

questions.q: Why did the director of the Bombay police refuse to give Fix an order of arrest?
choices: Only the London office could legally deliver the warrant
He did not believe that Fix was really a detective
He was a friend of Mr. Fogg from the Reform Club
He needed to see the stolen banknotes first
questions.evidence: the London office, which alone could legally deliver the warrant

questions.q: When Passepartout heard his master's orders at Bombay, what did he begin to wonder?
choices: Whether Fogg was secretly the bank robber
Whether the bet was really in good earnest
Whether Fix was really an agent of the steamer company
Whether he should quit and take a ship back to France
questions.evidence: He began to ask himself if this bet that Mr. Fogg talked about was not really in good earnest

questions.q: What was Passepartout watching in the streets of Bombay before he went to the pagoda?
choices: A Parsee festival with processions and dancing
A parade of soldiers marching to the fort
A large market where elephants were sold
Workmen building a new railway station
questions.evidence: It happened to be the day of a Parsee festival.

questions.q: What rule did Passepartout break by going into the pagoda on Malabar Hill?
choices: He went in during the hours it was closed to everyone
He did not leave his shoes outside the door first
He brought his package of new shirts and shoes inside
He touched the ornaments without asking the priests
questions.evidence: even the faithful must not go in without first leaving their shoes outside the door

questions.q: After Fogg spoke coldly to him, Passepartout was "quite crestfallen." What does crestfallen mean?
choices: Sad and ashamed
Angry and loud
Tired and sleepy
Proud and pleased
questions.evidence: Poor Passepartout, quite crestfallen, followed his master without a word.

questions.q: How did Passepartout arrive at the station at five minutes before eight?
choices: Calmly, carrying all the shirts and shoes he had bought
Hatless and shoeless, having lost his package
In a cab, with three angry priests chasing behind him
Holding the hand of Fix, who had led him back
questions.evidence: Passepartout, hatless, shoeless, and having in the squabble lost his package

questions.q: Why did Fix decide at the last moment to stay in Bombay instead of following Fogg onto the train?
choices: He had been ordered home by the police in London
An offence had been committed on Indian soil, so he could act
He thought the train was going in the wrong direction
He wanted to wait for the next steamer to Hong Kong
questions.evidence: An offence has been committed on Indian soil. I've got my man.
